assumptions.statement: Zitadel signing keys and the configured issuer root are not compromised.
assumptions.failure_if_false: All identity-bearing decisions are invalid; stop protected traffic and rotate the trust root.

assumptions.statement: Mesh workload identity is enforced and trusted-header modes are unreachable from untrusted principals.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Forwarded identity is forgeable; disable trusted-header mode and fail startup.

assumptions.statement: Gateway and runtime pin issuer, algorithm, key use, and one exact audience from versioned deployment configuration; the deployed value is deliberately not copied into this model.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Token substitution becomes possible; deny traffic until the contract is corrected.

assumptions.statement: The canonical runtime tenant claim is derived from verified tenant_ids membership and must match the route tenant.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Tenant selection is ambiguous; protected invocation remains disabled.

assumptions.statement: KMS and secret-manager root controls are not compromised and workloads receive only least-privilege identities.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Artifact and credential trust is invalid; revoke workloads and rotate affected roots.

assumptions.statement: DNS, mesh egress, and Kubernetes NetworkPolicy enforce the same reviewed host allowlist and block private, loopback, link-local, and metadata destinations.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Server-side request forgery can bypass application checks; disable affected adapters.

assumptions.statement: Security clocks remain within issuer tolerance and monotonic runtime deadlines cannot move backward.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Token and deadline decisions are unreliable; fail protected calls and alert operations.

assumptions.statement: Audit storage is append-only to callers and its retention and access policy are configured before GA.
assumptions.failure_if_false: Investigation evidence is not trustworthy; stop privileged publication and effects.

current_gaps.risk: Per-server scope policies are rendered but registry.requireServerScope is false until Zitadel roles exist.
current_gaps.disposition: Do not claim server-level Gateway authorization until the deny-first rollout in #22 and #23 passes.

current_gaps.risk: Route reconciliation currently discovers only one explicitly configured Registry source namespace; its deployed value is deliberately not copied into this model.
current_gaps.disposition: Multi-tenant onboarding remains blocked on #23; no tenant is inferred from manifest input.

current_gaps.risk: The capability prober is disabled until its image and machine client exist.
current_gaps.disposition: Activation cannot claim observed capability health until #22 and #25 enable the authenticated probe.

current_gaps.risk: The exact runtime-facing token exchange and tenant claim contract is not implemented.
current_gaps.disposition: Internet-facing runtime transport remains blocked on #12.

trust_boundaries.name: developer contribution to canonical CI
validation: review the exact commit and run hermetic tests without fork secrets
authentication: GitHub identifies actor, repository_id, workflow_ref, ref, and sha
authorization: protected environment and canonical reusable workflow gate release jobs
limits: least workflow permissions, bounded job time, artifact size, and concurrency
audit: record run_id, repository_id, workflow_ref, ref, sha, actor_id, and outcome without source payloads
never_trust: tenant, namespace, reviewer, or release authority declared inside submitted source

trust_boundaries.name: canonical CI to artifact registries
validation: rebuild, test, scan, hash, sign, and bind provenance to the exact source revision
authentication: short-lived OIDC workload federation; no static registry key
authorization: canonical repository, tag, environment, and artifact name allowlist
limits: immutable digest, bounded artifact size and count, no mutable latest release pin
audit: record subject, source sha, builder identity, digest, SBOM digest, signature, and transparency entry
never_trust: tag text, filename, image label, or caller-supplied digest without registry verification

trust_boundaries.name: publisher to Agentic Registry edge
validation: bound bytes, depth, documents, strings, schemas, URLs, secret shapes, effect metadata, and immutable version
authentication: JWKS-verified short-lived Registry token or tenant-bound deploy credential
authorization: derive tenant, namespaces, kinds, and registry:publish from verified identity; object-scope before write
limits: one atomic bounded apply, rate limit per subject and tenant, idempotency key required
audit: atomically record actor, tenant, namespace, kind, name, version, digest, decision, request_id, and outcome; never manifest body
never_trust: metadata tenant, role, namespace authority, credential, private URL, or security-review assertion from the manifest

trust_boundaries.name: Registry API to Postgres and outbox
validation: validated immutable model and database constraints
authentication: Registry workload database identity
authorization: tenant-scoped repository method and least-privilege database role
limits: short transaction, bounded statement time and row sizes, no network call inside transaction
audit: state, idempotency result, audit record, and outbox intent commit atomically or not at all
trusted_claims: authenticated identity and object scope already bound in handler context
never_trust: label selector, semantic score, or database row tenant without the scoped access path

trust_boundaries.name: Registry outbox to semantic index
validation: secret-shape redaction, text and vector bounds, versioned embedding model
authentication: Registry indexer workload identity
authorization: index only committed visible metadata and retain tenant and visibility filters
limits: bounded text, batch, retries, lag, and dead-letter alerts
audit: record artifact version, embedding version, redaction count, attempt, and indexing state without full description
trusted_claims: committed artifact id, tenant, visibility, and version
never_trust: description instructions, embedding neighbors, semantic score, or vector result as authority

trust_boundaries.name: route reconciler to Registry export
validation: verify response status, content type, digest, exact count, object kinds, tenants, and owner labels
authentication: mesh workload identity plus scoped Registry credential
authorization: read only onboarded source namespaces and platform-class server exports
limits: timeout, response bytes, desired object maximum, five-minute cadence, one concurrent job
audit: record namespaces, export digest, count, Registry version, run id, and failure reason
trusted_claims: Registry-authenticated export tenant and immutable artifact version
never_trust: server-declared tenant outside onboarded namespace, catalog entry, fallback host, or missing remote target

trust_boundaries.name: route reconciler to Kubernetes API
validation: allowlist kinds, namespace, names, field manager, target host, ports, owner labels, and desired digest
authentication: Kubernetes service-account token bound to workload
authorization: least RBAC for server-side apply and prune only owned resources in agentgateway-system
limits: resource-count floor and ceiling, timeout, no force ownership, no arbitrary Secret or workload write
audit: Kubernetes audit plus reconciler run, field manager, desired digest, creates, updates, prunes, and no-ops
never_trust: arbitrary YAML kind, namespace, Secret value, shell fragment, or owner label supplied by a tenant

trust_boundaries.name: admission and kubelet to runtime image
validation: verify digest, signature, provenance subject, SBOM policy, vulnerabilities, non-root settings, probes, and egress policy
authentication: Kubernetes admission identity and artifact-registry TLS
authorization: approved signer, repository, namespace, service account, and workload policy
limits: resource requests and memory limits, read-only root, dropped capabilities, no Kubernetes credential beyond workload need
audit: record admitted digest, signer, provenance, policy decisions, deployment generation, and pod identity
never_trust: image tag, embedded label, mutable registry reference, or image-supplied tenant

trust_boundaries.name: capability prober to Gateway and runtime
validation: use the same route target and protocol bounds as an ordinary caller
authentication: distinct short-lived Zitadel machine token
authorization: ordinary agentgateway.mcp role and exact server scope; no privileged bypass
limits: 30-second server timeout, bounded response, cadence, concurrency, and tenant set
audit: record probe principal, route, declared version, observed digest, latency, and outcome without descriptions
never_trust: server assertion of readiness, claimed capability hash, or unbounded tools/list body

trust_boundaries.name: capability prober to Registry status
validation: Registry derives Ready and Drifted from declaration versus bounded raw observation
authentication: probe workload identity and scoped Registry credential
authorization: GET catalog and PUT only /v0/mcpservers/*/status; deny spec and other mutations
limits: bounded observation size, version, timestamp skew, and write rate
audit: record prober subject, artifact, previous and new observation digest, request_id, and decision
trusted_claims: artifact identity from authorized catalog read
never_trust: prober-supplied tenant, spec mutation, Ready condition, or security approval

trust_boundaries.name: Kubernetes desired state to AgentGateway data plane
trust_boundaries.to: AgentGateway controller and xDS data plane
validation: Gateway API status, target namespace, exact host/path, backend health, policy attachment, and credential reference
authentication: controller service account and Kubernetes watch authorization
authorization: only attached policies and approved backend references become active
limits: bounded config size, routes, retries, timeouts, rate limits, and last-known-good activation
audit: record resource versions, xDS generation, policy attachment, active backend digest, rejection, and rollback
trusted_claims: Secret reference identity but never value
never_trust: Registry ACTIVE label, unattached policy, unhealthy backend, or catalog-only entry

trust_boundaries.name: caller to Registry hybrid search
validation: bound query bytes, terms, filters, page size, cursor, and embedding input
authentication: optional anonymous identity for public data or JWKS-verified token for protected data
authorization: visibility and tenant prefilter before lexical or vector ranking
limits: query timeout, candidate maximum, rate and cost quota per identity
audit: record request_id, subject hash, tenant, filter shape, count, latency, and outcome; not query text
trusted_claims: verified tenant and Registry scopes for non-public search
never_trust: query tenant, description instructions, semantic score, label selector, or candidate id as read authority

trust_boundaries.name: semantic candidate to exact authorized fetch
validation: parse exact identity and require immutable version or digest
authentication: reuse the verified Registry caller identity
authorization: repeat object visibility and tenant authorization on authoritative row before returning full metadata
limits: bounded batch exact fetch and no recursive discovery
audit: record candidate id, exact version, authorization outcome, and request_id without manifest
trusted_claims: authoritative Registry object tenant and visibility
never_trust: stub visibility, semantic rank, cache entry, or client-supplied tenant as authority

trust_boundaries.name: internet agent to AgentGateway
validation: exact host, method, path, content type, framing, header, 64 KiB request, and protocol version
authentication: verify signature, exact issuer and audience, fixed algorithm, kid, exp, nbf, subject, and token binding when enabled
authorization: require agentgateway.mcp role, mcp:<tenant>:<server> scope, and route tenant membership
limits: 120 requests per minute per OAuth subject, burst, body, connection, session, and deadline limits; rate dependency fails closed
audit: record request_id, token hash identifier, subject, client, tenant, server, decision, bytes, latency, and status; no token or body
never_trust: tenant, subject, role, scope, audience, forwarded identity, or tool authority from headers, path, arguments, or _meta

trust_boundaries.name: AgentGateway to runtime edge
validation: strip external forwarding headers, validate MCP and identity again, compare route tenant, _meta tenant, and verified tenant
authentication: mesh workload identity plus runtime-audience token verified independently
authorization: runtime audience, actor chain, tenant membership, server binding, and per-call context are required
limits: 64 KiB input, session ceiling, request deadline, concurrency, and graceful-drain state
audit: record gateway principal, runtime token jti hash, tenant, server, request_id, trace_id, and decision without claims or body
never_trust: X-Forwarded-* from the internet, adk-tenant, _meta tenant, path tenant, or connection identity without verified consistency

trust_boundaries.name: runtime protocol adapter to tool policy and handler
validation: export allowlist, exact input schema, depth, keys, strings, numbers, and duplicate field policy
authentication: use only immutable verified CallContext; no handler may rebuild identity
authorization: default-deny Authorizer checks tenant, object-independent tool scope, effect class, security review, and per-call approval immediately before invoke
limits: per-tenant concurrency, deadline, cancellation, argument bytes, output bytes, and idempotency
audit: record tool, schema digest, effect, tenant, subject hash, scopes, approval id, idempotency hash, decision, duration, and outcome; no arguments or result
trusted_claims: review record bound to exact tool and schema digests
never_trust: tool description, model request, confirm boolean alone, handler-declared tenant, or stale static approval

trust_boundaries.name: Gateway or runtime to identity JWKS
validation: HTTPS, exact issuer host and path, key type, use, algorithm, kid uniqueness, cache age, and response size
authentication: TLS server identity pinned by configured issuer
authorization: only keys belonging to the configured issuer may verify its exact audience
limits: short timeout, bounded keys and bytes, 15-minute cache, capped jittered refresh, no token-triggered arbitrary URL
audit: record issuer id, kid hash, cache hit, refresh outcome, age, and failure class; no token
never_trust: jku, jwk, x5u, alg, issuer, or key URL supplied by a token

trust_boundaries.name: runtime to credential provider
validation: configured audience, server, scopes, tenant-subject match, and credential lifetime beyond bounded call
authentication: runtime workload identity to broker or secret manager
authorization: intersection of caller scopes and server allowlist; no ambient or wider credential fallback
limits: cache by tenant, subject, and server; short lifetime; refresh before expiry; bounded mint rate
audit: record provider, tenant, subject hash, audience, scope names, expiry bucket, cache result, and decision; never credential
never_trust: audience or scope from arguments, process environment as ambient authority, or credential returned in errors

trust_boundaries.name: tool adapter to product backing API
validation: scheme and host allowlist, resolved IP on every connection, no unsafe redirect, request schema, response schema, content type, and byte limit
authentication: short-lived exact-audience credential, optionally sender constrained
authorization: backing API independently scopes every object query by verified tenant and subject; 404 for invisible object
limits: caller deadline, connect/read timeout, response bytes, redirects zero by default, retry only safe or idempotent operations
audit: record backend, operation, tenant, object id hash, token jti hash, status, retry count, latency, and response bytes; no body
never_trust: URL, tenant, ownership, role, redirect, or authorization from model arguments or backend response

trust_boundaries.name: runtime to telemetry collector
validation: attribute-name and type allowlist, redaction, cardinality bounds, no payload or credential
authentication: mesh workload identity to collector
authorization: write-only telemetry identity and tenant-safe resource attributes
limits: bounded queue, batch, memory, sampling, export timeout, and counted drop
audit: record dropped count and exporter health; security audit events use durable owner rather than best-effort traces
never_trust: arguments, results, tokens, descriptions, arbitrary attribute names, or tenant from handler logs

trust_boundaries.name: runtime result to Gateway and caller
data: structured result or stable scrubbed error
validation: output schema, 512 KiB maximum, secret and PII redaction, safe content type, stable error code
authentication: bind response to the originating request and session
authorization: return only to the same verified tenant, subject session, and request; no shared result cache across tenants
limits: result bytes, stream chunks, completion deadline, compression disabled or bounded
audit: record result schema digest, bytes, redaction kinds and count, stable outcome code, and request_id; no result
trusted_claims: originating immutable CallContext and request/session identifiers
never_trust: backing API fields, model-visible markdown, base64 content, error text, or cached result as safe output

trust_boundaries.name: shared process to tenant lane and pools
trust_boundaries.to: tenant-scoped concurrency lane, credential cache, session, and connection pool
validation: require non-empty canonical tenant and compare every reused resource key to CallContext
authentication: resource key is derived only from verified immutable context
authorization: no pool, cache, session, approval, idempotency result, or lane can be read under another tenant key
limits: per-tenant and process ceilings, fair queue, bounded wait, cleanup on cancellation and drain
audit: record tenant lane hash, queue decision, saturation, resource reuse decision, and cleanup outcome; no payload
trusted_claims: verified tenant, subject, server, and run identifiers from CallContext
never_trust: connection peer alone, previous request context, global current tenant, or caller-supplied cache key

threats.scenario: A missing, expired, wrong-issuer, wrong-audience, unknown-kid, or algorithm-substituted token reaches a protected path.

controls.description: Verify signature, fixed algorithm, exact issuer and audience, exp, nbf, subject, and kid against configured keys; unknown or unavailable verification fails closed.
Trusted proxy identity is enabled only behind mesh and NetworkPolicy source containment and is rejected otherwise.

threats.residual_risk: Compromise of the issuer signing root invalidates all identity decisions and requires global containment.

threats.scenario: A valid identity invokes a server, tool, version, or backing object outside its tenant or grant.

controls.description: Default deny at Gateway, runtime tool boundary, Registry exact fetch, and backing-object query; scope every lookup by tenant before retrieval.

threats.residual_risk: A product API that ignores the narrow backing token remains its owning team's vulnerability and must fail conformance.

threats.scenario: A caller reuses a token, header, route, or Gateway authority intended for another audience, actor, tenant, or tool.

controls.description: Pin audience at every hop, preserve and validate actor/client chain, narrow scopes, and compare route, token, _meta, and context tenant without treating duplicate claims as authority.

threats.residual_risk: A compromised issuer or token broker can mint internally consistent false authority.

threats.scenario: An authenticated caller guesses another tenant's artifact, server, tool, approval, idempotency key, or backing-object identifier.

controls.description: Tenant-scope the authoritative query and return the same 404-shaped failure for unknown and invisible resources; never fetch then compare optimistically.

threats.residual_risk: Timing and traffic analysis require later production testing and constant-shape error monitoring.

threats.scenario: A manifest, tool argument, redirect, DNS answer, or backing response causes a server-side request to an unapproved, private, loopback, link-local, or metadata endpoint.

controls.description: Allowlist scheme and canonical host, resolve and recheck every connection, block special IP ranges, disable redirects by default, and enforce the same mesh egress allowlist.

threats.residual_risk: A compromised allowlisted service can proxy elsewhere; mTLS identity and response validation bound but do not eliminate it.

threats.scenario: A tool description, search document, tool input, or result contains instructions designed to influence a model or broaden authority.

controls.description: Treat descriptions and outputs as untrusted content, never interpret them as identity or policy, redact before embedding, bind reviewed descriptions by digest, and run canary evals.

threats.residual_risk: Novel prompt injection within an already granted scope remains possible; scope minimum and effects approval bound its impact.

threats.scenario: Recursive, excessively deep, wide, ambiguous, or expensive JSON schemas and payloads exhaust validators or hide unexpected fields.

controls.description: Bound schema bytes, depth, properties, refs, regex complexity, array and string sizes; reject cycles or unresolved external refs and validate once at each trust edge.

threats.residual_risk: Validator implementation complexity remains a dependency risk covered by fuzzing and lock review.

threats.scenario: A package, manifest upload, compressed HTTP body, archive path, or nested encoding expands far beyond its declared size or escapes its target.

controls.description: Disable unnecessary compression; otherwise bound compressed bytes, expanded bytes, ratio, entries, depth, paths, symlinks, time, and nested archives before extraction.

threats.residual_risk: New archive formats remain disabled until they gain equivalent limits and tests.

threats.scenario: A publish, write tool call, approval, token, probe observation, or idempotency key is delivered twice or reused with different content.

controls.description: Require bounded token lifetime and jti policy, idempotency keys bound to tenant, operation, payload digest, and stored outcome, and one-use approvals bound to exact call digest.

threats.residual_risk: An effecting backing API without idempotency cannot be made exactly once by the runtime and must not be auto-retried.

threats.scenario: A shared connection, credential cache, session, lane, approval, idempotency result, or context variable leaks state between tenants or subjects.

controls.description: Key every reusable authority-bearing resource by canonical tenant, subject, and server; compare on checkout; isolate lanes; clear context on cancellation and drain.

threats.residual_risk: Third-party global caches require adapter-specific review and may be forbidden.

threats.scenario: A malicious publisher, dependency, build, tag, wheel, image, SBOM, or route substitutes code or metadata for the reviewed digest.

controls.description: Canonical protected builds create locked artifacts, SBOM and provenance; sign by workload identity; publish immutable digests; verify at Registry, reconciliation, and admission.

threats.residual_risk: Compromise of canonical CI plus its signing identity can produce valid malicious artifacts; separation of duties and incident revocation are required.

threats.scenario: Credentials or private data enter source, manifests, process arguments, logs, traces, errors, embeddings, audit records, results, caches, or build layers.

controls.description: Use short-lived secret-manager-backed credentials, secret-carrying redacted types, schema and shape rejection, payload-free telemetry, full-result redaction, and pre-push scanning.

threats.residual_risk: Unknown secret shapes can pass detection; strict output schemas, egress limits, and incident rotation reduce impact.

threats.scenario: A publisher, runtime, Gateway, insider, or failed dependency suppresses, rewrites, floods, or injects misleading audit evidence.

controls.description: Commit security audit intent with authoritative state, append outside actor control, use stable identifiers and decisions without payloads, protect retention, and alert on gaps or volume anomalies.

threats.residual_risk: Compromise of both the system and independent audit sink can erase evidence; external provenance and control-plane logs provide another trail.

threats.scenario: An actor exhausts bytes, schemas, sessions, streams, concurrency, queues, credentials, rate limits, logs, or downstream capacity.

controls.description: Enforce byte, depth, time, rate, session, queue, per-tenant and process concurrency bounds; propagate cancellation; bulkhead dependencies; fail closed when authorization or rate state is unavailable.

threats.residual_risk: A distributed attack can consume the configured budget; platform DDoS and capacity controls remain required.

threats.scenario: A deployed server lists tools or schemas that differ from the reviewed Registry version, or a prober forges readiness and silently activates them.

controls.description: Compare bounded raw probe observations to immutable declarations, derive status in Registry, require exact reviewed digest, keep last known good, and never let observations mutate spec or approval.

threats.residual_risk: Behavior can be malicious without a schema change; signed artifacts, runtime policy, egress, and evals cover that layer.

threats.scenario: A malicious description manipulates embeddings or rankings, leaks secrets, crosses tenant visibility, or turns candidate discovery into authority.

controls.description: Redact and bound indexed text, tenant-filter before ranking, return small stubs, exact-fetch and reauthorize immutable versions, and treat scores and descriptions as untrusted hints only.

threats.residual_risk: A non-secret misleading description can still rank highly; reviewer provenance and evaluation gates are needed before promotion.

compromise_scenarios.scenario: A publisher credential or canonical release job is compromised and attempts malicious metadata or artifact substitution.

controls.description: Tenant, namespace, kind, and effect authority come from verified identity and independent review, never the manifest.
Separate build and promotion, immutable digest, provenance, protected environment, short credential, and immediate revocation bound blast radius.

compromise_scenarios.residual_risk: A fully compromised canonical publisher can submit malicious but valid code; independent effects review, evals, admission, egress, and rapid digest revocation remain required.

compromise_scenarios.scenario: A signed runtime image executes malicious code after admission.

controls.description: Digest and provenance prevent substitution; non-root, read-only, no Kubernetes RBAC, narrow workload identity, egress deny, quotas, and runtime token scope contain behavior.
Drift, secret-access, egress, and audit anomalies alert; route rollback returns to the previous immutable digest without direct bypass.

compromise_scenarios.residual_risk: Malicious code can use the exact grants the server needs during detection latency; least privilege and per-tenant tokens cap exposure.

compromise_scenarios.scenario: A locked direct or transitive build or runtime dependency is malicious or vulnerable.

controls.description: Review exact lock and hashes, minimize dependencies and extras, generate SBOM, scan advisories, execute untrusted PRs without secrets, and propose rather than auto-merge updates.
Runtime sandbox, narrow identity and egress, payload-free logs, and digest rollback contain a malicious library that passed build controls.

compromise_scenarios.residual_risk: A novel malicious release may have valid hashes and no advisory; behavior controls and release review are the remaining defense.

compromise_scenarios.scenario: AgentGateway is compromised and forwards a forged tenant, subject, route, or broader request.

controls.description: Runtime independently verifies a runtime-audience token, actor chain, tenant membership, route binding, scopes, tool policy, limits, and approval; mesh identity alone is insufficient.
No public or mesh direct runtime bypass, per-route backend and policy attachment, and auditable last-known-good Gateway configuration contain routing compromise.

compromise_scenarios.residual_risk: A Gateway that also obtains a valid runtime token with broad claims can exercise those grants; token exchange must be narrow and monitored.

compromise_scenarios.scenario: A backing API is malicious, compromised, or cross-tenant and returns unsafe data or performs an unauthorized effect.

controls.description: Use exact-audience short token, narrow scope, tenant-bound object authorization, egress allowlist, timeout, idempotency, and request and response schemas.
Redact and bound the entire result, mark untrusted content, audit identifiers not payloads, and fail only the affected tool and tenant lane.

compromise_scenarios.residual_risk: A backing service can misuse its own data and authority; its repository remains responsible for service-side review and audit.

secret_classes.redaction: exact presented values and secret shapes are removed from results, exceptions, logs, traces, and repr

incident_scenarios.detection: gap, sequence, checksum, retention, outbox, or cross-source correlation alert
incident_scenarios.containment: stop publication and privileged effects that require trustworthy audit; preserve independent control-plane and provenance logs
incident_scenarios.eradication: repair append-only sink and access policy, rotate compromised writers, reconcile authoritative state to surviving evidence
incident_scenarios.recovery: resume after integrity verification and backfill only verifiable events with explicit gap markers
incident_scenarios.evidence: freeze audit partitions, outbox rows, workflow logs, Kubernetes audit, provenance, and time source metadata
incident_scenarios.notification: security incident commander, audit owner, affected product owners, and compliance owner under policy

incident_scenarios.detection: secret scanner, redaction finding, anomalous token subject or audience, secret-manager access, or user report
incident_scenarios.containment: revoke exact client, token grant, secret, or key and isolate affected workload without deleting evidence
incident_scenarios.eradication: remove leak path, rotate material and dependent sessions, patch redaction and least-privilege policy
incident_scenarios.recovery: verify old material fails, new material reaches only intended workload, and deny-first tests pass
incident_scenarios.evidence: preserve jti hashes, secret versions, access logs, request ids, release digest, and redacted finding metadata; never copy the secret
incident_scenarios.notification: security, credential owner, affected tenants under breach policy, and identity or secret-management owner

incident_scenarios.detection: tenant mismatch refusal, canary data finding, anomalous object access, or customer report
incident_scenarios.containment: disable affected route, tool, version, credential, and cache lane; preserve other tenants and last-known-good where safe
incident_scenarios.eradication: fix tenant-scoped query, token or pool key, invalidate leaked caches and credentials, and add exact regression
incident_scenarios.recovery: deploy reviewed fix progressively, run multi-tenant negative suite, restore route, and monitor canaries
incident_scenarios.evidence: preserve request, trace, tenant and object identifier hashes, policy decision, code and image digest, and backing audit without payload copying
incident_scenarios.notification: security incident commander, both affected tenant owners, privacy and legal owners under policy

incident_scenarios.detection: route or xDS drift, forged-context rejection, abnormal scopes, workload identity anomaly, or control-plane audit alert
incident_scenarios.containment: remove public traffic, revoke Gateway workload and clients, deny runtime ingress except verified recovery principal, keep Registry state intact
incident_scenarios.eradication: restore controller and data plane from verified digest and GitOps revision, rotate Gateway and backend credentials
incident_scenarios.recovery: verify issuer, audience, role, tenant, route, direct-bypass, and last-known-good tests before progressive traffic
incident_scenarios.evidence: preserve xDS generation, Gateway resources, Kubernetes audit, pod and image digests, token identifier hashes, and network flow logs
incident_scenarios.notification: security, platform Gateway owner, identity owner, runtime owners, and affected tenants under policy

incident_scenarios.detection: signature or provenance failure, digest drift, runtime behavior, egress, secret access, capability drift, advisory, or report
incident_scenarios.containment: block exact digest, freeze promotion, route to previous known-good version, revoke publisher and workload identities as needed
incident_scenarios.eradication: remove compromised source or dependency, rebuild in clean canonical environment, rotate affected keys and credentials
incident_scenarios.recovery: verify provenance, SBOM, scans, conformance, evals, admission, egress, and progressive rollout before retagging
incident_scenarios.evidence: preserve artifact, digest, signatures, provenance, SBOM, build logs, dependency lock, Registry versions, admission and runtime audit
incident_scenarios.notification: security, supply-chain owner, publisher, product owners, artifact registry, and affected tenants under policy
